title: A Current for the Rivergate
premise: Wren Voss, a desert ranger who survives by never stopping, is hired to find a vanished government survey team near the Rivergate, a drowned ruin where the desert meets a dead sea. The team left behind intact gear and no tracks, evidence of something that erases people rather than kills them. Racing a ruthless salvage fleet commander who wants the ruin's water-technology for himself, Wren gathers a ragtag crew of strays she never meant to keep. She discovers the survey team was taken by the ruin's living current, a power that offers survival at the price of becoming part of it, and that her missing brother chose that trade years ago. In the end Wren refuses the current's bargain, breaks its hold by giving up the salvage prize, and chooses her found family over the survival she's always run toward.
about_author: Silas Amberdale is the pen name of a former field cartographer who spent a decade mapping arid basins before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people who keep moving, and what finally makes them stop.

chapters.title: Six Tides of Dust
chapters.summary: Wren Voss tracks a petty thief across the flats, catching him only because stopping costs more than chasing. A government courier intercepts her with a contract: find the vanished Meridian survey team at the Rivergate. POV Wren. Beat: restless competence masking exhaustion.

chapters.title: Gear Without Graves
chapters.summary: At the survey camp Wren finds tents pitched, meals half-eaten, instruments running — and no tracks in any direction, including the sand inside the tents. Her tracker instincts fail for the first time. POV Wren. Beat: professional confidence cracking into unease.

chapters.title: The Fleet on the Horizon
chapters.summary: Salvage ships appear on the dead sea, led by Commander Ilsa Brann of the Korvane fleet, who claims the government contract is void and the wreck is hers. Wren realizes she has six tides before the fleet reaches the Rivergate. POV Wren. Beat: the race begins.

chapters.title: A Boy Who Steals Boats
chapters.summary: Wren catches Tam, a river-orphan stowaway, stealing her supplies; he knows hidden channels to the Rivergate she doesn't. She tells herself he's a means to an end. POV Tam. Beat: wary first alliance, humor against danger.

chapters.title: What the Water Remembers
chapters.summary: Crossing the salt flats, the crew finds a survivor: surveyor Denna Okoro, half-mad, repeating that the current 'asked her name.' She carries a survey journal describing a machine beneath the ruin. POV Wren. Beat: dread deepens, first real mystery.

chapters.title: Brann's Offer
chapters.summary: Brann catches Wren's crew and offers partnership: Wren's tracking for a share of salvage. Wren refuses, sensing Brann discards people who stop being useful. They escape using Tam's channels. POV Wren. Beat: moral line drawn, enemy established.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Daughter
chapters.summary: In a drifting fishing village, old ferryman Sef recognizes Wren's surname — and reveals her brother Joss passed through years ago, heading for the Rivergate, never returning. POV Sef. Beat: the personal stakes surface; grief she'd buried.

chapters.title: Into the Drowned Streets
chapters.summary: The crew enters the Rivergate's flooded avenues at low tide, following the survey journal through submerged markets. The water moves against the wind. POV Tam. Beat: wonder curdling to fear; found family tightening.

chapters.title: The Asking
chapters.summary: The current speaks to Wren — not words, but offers: her brother's voice, rest, an end to running. Denna nearly walks back into the water. Wren drags her out. POV Wren. Beat: temptation made intimate.

chapters.title: Joss's Mark
chapters.summary: Deep in the ruin they find carvings in Wren's family's ranger-sign: Joss is alive inside the current, part of it, and he's been leaving warnings for years. POV Wren. Beat: hope and horror entwined.

chapters.title: Half the Fleet
chapters.summary: Brann's advance team enters the ruin; the current takes three of them in front of Wren's crew. Brann, unmoved, accelerates her salvage timetable. POV Brann. Beat: villain's cold arithmetic; the cost of power.

chapters.title: The Machine Under the Gate
chapters.summary: The journal's coordinates lead to the heart: an ancient engine that harvests people into the current, built by a civilization that traded its citizens for water. The survey team is in the mechanism, still conscious. POV Denna. Beat: the theme made literal — survival powered by sacrifice.

chapters.title: Tide Four
chapters.summary: With two tides left, the crew argues: destroy the machine and lose the water technology the dying villages need, or let Brann take it and feed it. Tam sides with Wren; Denna wavers, hearing her lost team in the current. POV Tam. Beat: fracture and loyalty.

chapters.title: What Brann Buried
chapters.summary: A captured fleet engineer reveals Brann's Korvane is dying of thirst — she needs the machine to save her own city, and doesn't care what it consumes. POV Brann. Beat: the villain becomes sympathetic without becoming right.

chapters.title: The Current's Bargain
chapters.summary: The current offers Wren a trade: Joss freed, her crew guaranteed water, if she takes her brother's place in the engine. She almost says yes. POV Wren. Beat: the price of survival made personal and unbearable.

chapters.title: Tam's Channels
chapters.summary: Tam discovers the machine's intake runs through the channels only river-orphans know — a way to flood the engine with open sea and drown its hunger. But it requires someone to open the deep gates from inside. POV Tam. Beat: the boy becomes the linchpin; courage.

chapters.title: Tide Five
chapters.summary: Brann's main force arrives and storms the ruin. In the chaos, Denna walks into the current to rejoin her team, and Wren lets her go — the first time she's ever let anyone choose to stop. POV Wren. Beat: grief, respect, the cost of agency.

chapters.title: The Gates Below
chapters.summary: Wren and Joss, half-dissolved into the current, meet inside the machine. He begs her to take the bargain; she refuses and instead shows him Tam's plan. He chooses to open the gates himself. POV Joss. Beat: brotherhood, release, the climax's hinge.

chapters.title: Sixth Tide
chapters.summary: The gates open; open sea floods the engine. The current's voice becomes a scream, then silence. Wren drags Joss's body from the water as Brann's fleet retreats from the collapsing ruin. POV Wren. Beat: climax — victory paid in full.

chapters.title: Ash and Salt
chapters.summary: Brann, broken but alive, accepts water from the villages' old wells instead — enough, if shared. Wren gives up her salvage claim to fund it. The survey team is buried with names. POV Brann. Beat: power unclenched; imperfect peace.

chapters.title: The Ranger Who Stopped
chapters.summary: Wren takes the crew — Tam, Sef, the freed survivors — to the river villages, and for the first time in years, stays. She buries Joss's ranger badge and plants a marker. POV Wren. Beat: stillness chosen, not imposed.

chapters.title: A Current for the Rivergate
chapters.summary: A year later, the Rivergate is a mapped, guarded ruin where the water runs clean and slow. Tam trains new guides; Wren teaches rangers that stopping isn't dying. The current is quiet — but the last line notes the tide still turns. POV Wren. Beat: earned resolution, open horizon.
